executive_summary: Markets enter Tuesday with conflicting signals: Asia rallied 1.7% overnight led by chipmakers, and S&P 500 futures point higher at 7,458 as Iran peace-talk hopes offset fresh U.S. airstrikes. The semiconductor sector, which shed $3.3 trillion after Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 triggered a bear market, is attempting a technical bounce from deeply oversold levels. However, Yemen's Houthis declaring a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia adds a dangerous new dimension to already-elevated oil prices ($82 WTI, $88 Brent), with U.S. crude inventories at a 45-year low of just 43 days of supply. Earnings season accelerates with GM, Novartis, Northrop Grumman, and 70 other companies reporting today, while GOOGL, TSLA, and INTC loom later this week as the defining tests for whether the AI trade can resume.

macro_events.title: Houthi Maritime Embargo on Saudi Arabia + Fresh U.S. Strikes on Iran
macro_events.causal_chain: Yemen's Houthis declare maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia effective immediately → Saudi exports ~4.5M bbl/day from Yanbu through Bab al-Mandab Strait now at risk → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs transiting Red Sea → Brent-WTI spread widens as Asian refiners face supply disruption → U.S. SPR at 45-year low (43 days supply) limits government's ability to cushion price spikes → if Saudi reroutes via Cape of Good Hope, adds 12-14 days and ~$2M per trip → European natgas (TTF futures) at risk if LNG from Qatar redirected → 9th consecutive night of U.S. strikes further escalates retaliation risk → Iran peace-talk proposals offer potential off-ramp but Baghaei's 'resolute defense' rhetoric suggests no near-term deal
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Red Sea, global shipping lanes, U.S. fuel prices
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent spiked 15% in 24 hours. Current situation more sustained but lower intensity; markets pricing ~$82-88 vs. $112 spring highs, suggesting controlled escalation premium
macro_events.counterargument: Iran's acknowledgment of peace proposals suggests diplomatic off-ramp exists. Brent remains well below spring $112 highs, indicating markets view supply disruption as manageable. Saudi Arabia may not enforce Houthi demands.

macro_events.title: Moonshot AI Kimi K3 Triggers $3.3T Semiconductor Wipeout — Bear Market Bounce Attempt
macro_events.causal_chain: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 (2.8T parameter open-weight model) matches top U.S. AI systems on coding benchmarks → exposes assumption that expensive GPU compute would stay scarce → SOX falls 24% from June record, entering bear market → $3.3T in chip sector value destroyed in three weeks → SOX and Nasdaq-100 now technically oversold → Asian chipmakers rally 2.5%+ overnight Monday → SOX opens +2% Tuesday on mean-reversion trade → BUT validation requires GOOGL/INTC earnings later this week to confirm CapEx guidance → if hyperscalers signal spending cuts, bear market deepens; if they raise guidance, V-shaped recovery possible → Trump admin reportedly considering ban on Chinese AI models (Axios), which could provide geopolitical floor for U.S. chip names
macro_events.geographic_dimension: U.S., China, South Korea, Taiwan — global AI supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: Jan 2025 DeepSeek moment — similar Chinese AI efficiency shock wiped ~$1T from chip stocks but recovered within 2 weeks as hyperscaler spending proved resilient. Current selloff is deeper (24% vs ~17%) suggesting more sustained repricing
macro_events.counterargument: TSMC just committed $100B additional U.S. investment citing multi-year demand megatrend. FactSet tracking 52% S&P 500 EPS growth in Q2. Citi says Mag 7 framework is dead but underlying AI spend continues accelerating. Open-weight models don't eliminate need for training compute.

macro_events.title: Section 301 Tariff Actions — Brazil 25% July 22, Forced-Labor Tariffs on 60 Countries
macro_events.causal_chain: USTR imposes 25% tariff on all Brazilian imports effective July 22 → USTR forced-labor investigation completion deadline was July 20 → proposed 10-12.5% tariffs on imports from 60 countries including Canada, EU, Mexico, Indonesia → 10% global IEEPA surcharge expires by statute July 24 → net tariff regime may shift significantly this week → combined with China's 23.4% effective rate, global trade costs rising → consumer price impacts lag by 2-3 months → supply chain rerouting accelerates → Brazilian coffee, soybeans, steel, aircraft parts most affected → Mexico nearshoring thesis weakened if forced-labor tariff applied
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — Brazil, China, EU, Canada, Mexico, 60 countries total
macro_events.historical_analog: 2018-2019 trade war escalation — initial tariff rounds caused ~6% S&P 500 drawdown before markets adjusted. Current situation involves broader scope (60 countries) but lower rates (10-12.5% vs. 25% China tariffs)
macro_events.counterargument: IEEPA surcharge expiration July 24 may partially offset new Section 301 tariffs. Markets have already priced significant trade uncertainty since 2025. Companies have had time to diversify supply chains.

macro_events.title: Fed Quiet Period — Rate Hold Expected but September Hike Odds Rising to 53%
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed holds at 3.5-3.75% with 88% probability of pause at July meeting → June CPI dropped 0.4% (largest since April 2020) suggesting inflation cooling → BUT oil at $82+ WTI and Houthi Saudi embargo threaten energy-driven inflation resurgence → markets now pricing 53% chance of September rate HIKE (up from 47%) → 10Y Treasury yield climbed to 4.60% reflecting rate uncertainty → higher yields pressure equity valuations especially growth/tech → TIPS auction this week will signal inflation protection demand
macro_events.historical_analog: 2022 energy-driven inflation cycle — oil above $100 forced aggressive Fed hiking. Current situation less extreme but direction similar.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI was flat in June, suggesting underlying inflation well-controlled. Oil price spikes may prove transitory if Iran peace talks resume. Fed's own task forces suggest institutional focus on longer-term framework.
